from.place: the d=0 irreducible case in the 02UZ induction: identify sections of a constant sheaf on every nonempty open

title: Sections of a constant sheaf on an irreducible space
statement: Let X be an irreducible topological space and A an abelian group. On the site of open subsets of X with open coverings [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], let A_X be the constant abelian sheaf, namely the sheafification of the constant presheaf with value A [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every nonempty open subset U of X, the sections A_X(U) are canonically A, and for nonempty opens V subseteq U the restriction map A_X(U) \to A_X(V) is the identity under these identifications.

source.place: Definition 006W (definition-constant-sheaf), together with the locally constant-map description of the associated sheaf

proof.text: If U is nonempty and open in the irreducible space X, then U is irreducible: two nonempty open subsets of U are also nonempty open subsets of X and therefore meet. Thus irreducibility is inherited by every nonempty open.

source.place: Definition 004V and the irreducible-open-subspace observation used in Proposition 02UZ

proof.text: Let L_A be the presheaf of locally constant A-valued maps on the open subsets of X, an abelian group under pointwise addition with restriction of maps. By [lem-weil-pbc-locally-constant-maps-sheaf], L_A is a sheaf (the sheaf condition concerns the underlying sets, and glued maps of sums are sums of glued maps). Let P be the constant presheaf U \mapsto A and c: P \to L_A the morphism sending a \in A to the constant map with value a. We check that (L_A, c) has the universal property of the sheafification in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. Let G be an abelian sheaf and phi: P \to G a morphism. Existence: for f in L_A(U), choose an open cover U = \bigcup U_i with f constant of value a_i on U_i; the sections phi_{U_i}(a_i) agree on each U_i \cap U_j because f has a single value there (or the overlap is empty) and phi commutes with restriction, so they glue to a unique section psi_U(f) of G(U), independent of the cover (compare on a common refinement); psi is additive and commutes with restriction, and psi \circ c = phi. Uniqueness: two morphisms L_A \to G that agree after composing with c agree on constant maps, hence on every f in L_A(U) locally on a cover where f is constant, hence on f since G is a sheaf. Therefore (L_A, c) is a sheafification of P, and the unique isomorphism of universal objects identifies A_X with L_A compatibly with the maps from P. Thus A_X(U) is canonically the group of locally constant maps U \to A, and restriction to V \subseteq U is restriction of maps.

source.place: Definition 006W and Example 0081 (sheafification of the constant presheaf)

proof.text: By [lem-pc-irreducible-space-connected], irreducibility of U implies that U is connected; since U is nonempty, [lem-weil-pbc-connected-locally-constant-map] says every locally constant map U \to A is constant. Hence evaluation at any point of U identifies A_X(U) canonically with A.

source.place: Definition 004V and the irreducible d=0 argument in cohomology Proposition 02UZ

proof.text: For nonempty opens V subseteq U, the restriction of a constant map with value a is the same constant map with value a. Therefore the canonical identifications A_X(U) = A and A_X(V) = A carry the restriction map to the identity of A.
